title: Spaghetti Aglio e Olio
short: Garlic, olive oil, chili and pasta water turned into a silky sauce. Pantry magic.
keywords: Spaghetti Aglio e Olio, date night, dinner for two, cozy, playful
intro: Aglio e olio is the late-night Roman classic that proves impressive doesn't mean expensive. With garlic, olive oil, chili and starchy pasta water you can build a glossy sauce that clings to every strand. Technique carries the whole dish, which makes it a quietly brilliant way to show you can cook.
why: It is cheap, fast and made from pantry staples, but the emulsified, glossy sauce looks like it came from a trattoria.

video.title: Pasta aglio e olio from the movie Chef

ings.h: 200 g (7 oz)

ings.i: kosher salt, for the pasta water

ings.h: 60 ml (¼ cup)

ings.i: lemon zest, plus a squeeze of juice
grated Parmesan, to serve (optional; not vegan)

steps.t: Bring 2 liters (2 quarts) of water to a boil with the salt. Using less water than usual concentrates the starch you need for the sauce. Cook the spaghetti for 2 minutes less than the package says.
Meanwhile, put the oil and garlic in a cold, large skillet and set over medium-low heat. Cook 4–6 minutes, swirling, until the garlic edges are pale gold. Add the chili for 30 seconds.
Add a ladle (about 120 ml / ½ cup) of pasta water to the skillet to stop the garlic cooking.

Use tongs to move the spaghetti straight into the skillet with another splash of water. Toss hard over medium-high heat for 1–2 minutes until the liquid turns into a glossy sauce that coats the pasta.
Off the heat, add the parsley, lemon zest and juice. Taste for salt and twirl into nests on warm plates.

tips: The toss is the technique. Vigorous movement plus starch plus fat equals emulsion.
If the pasta looks dry, add pasta water a tablespoon at a time. It should look saucy, not oily.
makeahead: Slice the garlic and chop the parsley ahead; this dish is cooked to order.
plating: Twirl each portion with tongs inside a ladle, slide onto the plate as a tall nest, and finish with a few chili flakes and a drizzle of oil.

faq.a: Too little starch or not enough tossing. Add a splash of pasta water and toss hard over the heat again.
